as_told.title: Bob Jacobs films a UFO knocking down an Atlas warhead
as_told.place_text: Vandenberg Air Force Base / Big Sur, California

plain: In 1964, a man named Bob Jacobs worked as a photo instrumentation specialist, filming missile tests from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. According to the tellings, he was about 100 miles up the coast at Big Sur with a telescope camera aimed at an Atlas missile carrying a dummy nuclear warhead. When the film was reviewed, they say, an object flew into the frame, chased the warhead at 6,000 to 8,000 miles an hour, circled it, fired a beam of light at it, and the warhead went down. If true, something unknown can knock out a nuclear weapon in flight. The podcast host Jesse Michels retells it many times, citing a researcher of UFOs and nuclear weapons, Robert Hastings, and Jacobs' DD214, his military discharge record. Ross Coulthart cites an Omni magazine article and puts the launch near Edwards instead, and a filmmaker, James Fox, also brings it up. Some tellings say only that the object circled the missile and was filmed, without saying it brought the warhead down.
